title: The Fall of Man
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The fall of man means that humanity rebelled against God through Adam and Eve’s sin, bringing guilt, corruption, death, and separation into the human race. The world is broken because sin entered God’s good creation.
summary: The fall of man means that humanity rebelled against God through Adam and Eve’s sin, bringing guilt, corruption, death, and separation into the human race. The world is broken because sin entered God’s good creation.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the promised Savior who defeats the serpent, reverses the ruin of the fall, and restores sinners to God. Where Adam failed, Christ obeyed and brings life to His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The fall explains why the world is not as it should be. God created good, but humanity rebelled against His Word. Adam and Eve distrusted God, listened to deception, and disobeyed His command.

Sin brought shame, fear, blame, pain, toil, conflict, death, and exile from Eden. The fall was not a small mistake; it was rebellion against the Creator and the entrance of corruption into human life.

The fall also introduced conflict with the serpent and the need for redemption. God’s judgment was real, but even in Genesis 3, He promised that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent’s head.

Christ is the answer to the fall. He came to destroy the works of the devil, obey where humanity failed, bear sin’s curse, and restore His people to life with God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without the fall, people misdiagnose the human condition. They may blame only environment, systems, weakness, ignorance, or trauma while missing humanity’s rebellion against God.

This doctrine tells the truth about the brokenness everyone sees and feels. Death, shame, temptation, relational conflict, and suffering are not normal parts of God’s original design; they are part of sin’s ruin, which Christ came to overcome.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat sin as harmless or creation’s brokenness as meaningless. Grieve what sin has ruined, take temptation seriously, and look to Christ as the promised Redeemer. Let the story of the fall teach humility, repentance, and hope in God’s restoring grace.
